question.text: In the 20th century, this Southern Hemisphere country built a nearly 3500-mile fence to keep dingos, a type of wild dog that lives in this country's outback, out of its more populated southeast.
question.clue: In this country, the murder of James Scobie at Ballarat led to an insurrection of gold miners in the Eureka Rebellion.

swap.text: The "history wars" began after the Bringing Them Home report was released on these people. This term refers to Australian Aborigines taken from their families as children by the Australian government.
swap.clue: An official 2007 apology to these people and their descendants was made by then-Prime Minister Kevin Rudd.

question.leadin: This colony was founded by the First Fleet on January 26, 1788, and its first governor was Arthur Phillip.
question.text: Name this colony which originated around Port Jackson. Lachlan Macquarie was the final governor of this territory.
question.clue: George Johnston and John Macarthur led forces during an 1808 event in this colony.

swap.text: This man has hidden in an Ecuadorian embassy since 2012, a saga stemming from sexual assault charges now dropped. His 2010 talk was "Why the World Needs Wikileaks".
swap.clue: Daniel Ellsberg praised this man, saying his actions were similar to Ellsberg's handling of the Pentagon Papers.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the failure of the Gallipoli Campaign.
question.text: The date of the Gallipoli landing is a day of remembrance for this expeditionary force, which was composed of soldiers from two British commonwealths.
question.answerHtml: ANZAC [or the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps]
question.clue: Their most notable action is remembered in the song titled "And the Band Played" a certain nationalist folk tune, was supported by the French from Kum Kale, and was advocated by Winston Churchill.

swap.leadin: Australia has struggled with the civil rights of these people.
swap.text: These indigenous Australians were frequently massacred at the beginning of British colonization of Australia.
swap.clue: These victims of the Myall Creek massacre were also targeted in the Black War.

question.leadin: As Treasurer of Australia, this man oversaw the creation of the Australian Dollar and later ended the pegging of the currency to the British pound.
question.text: Name this Prime Minister who more famously went missing while swimming at Cheviot Beach in 1967. Ironically, a swimming pool in Melbourne was named in his honor.
question.clue: This prime minister declared that he was "all the way with LBJ" in showing his country's support for the Vietnam War.

swap.leadin: Peter Lalor was one leader of this event, and each of its thirteen participants who were tried for treason were acquitted.
swap.text: Name this rebellion by gold miners against the British colonial administration of Victoria.
swap.answerHtml: Eureka Stockade [or Eureka Rebellion; accept equivalents for “Rebellion” such as “Revolt”]
swap.clue: It was partly incited by the acquittal of James Bentley, whose hotel was burned to the ground, leading Robert Rede to request additional troops from Charles Hotham, whose dispatches are a key source on this event.

question.text: The band Midnight Oil wore jackets with "SORRY" on the back to draw attention to the Stolen Generations during the 2000 Summer Olympics in this Australian city. This is the most populous city in Australia.
question.clue: Lachlan Macquarie ("LACK-lan muh-KWAIR-ee") was placed in charge of this city after John Macarthur overthrew governor William Bligh in the Rum Rebellion.

swap.leadin: During World War II, the US 1st Marine Division adopted this ballad by Banjo Paterson as their official march.
swap.text: Name this song, which "the Band Played" in an Eric Bogle song memorializing the Gallipoli campaign. It is considered Australia's "unofficial national anthem."
swap.clue: While at an outback station, Banjo Paterson wrote this "unofficial Australian anthem" which describes a "jolly swagman camped by a billabong." This song's title refers to the motion of a "tucker bag" containing a "jumbuck."

question.leadin: Answer the following about the "White Australia" policy of discrimination.
question.text: This prime minister of Australia during World War Two, a member of the Labour Party, defended the policy by declaring the country "the home of the British race" in a 1942 speech.
question.clue: Later, New Zealand and Australia laid out their post-WWII military and political goals in the Canberra Pact, signed by this Australian prime minister. Frank Forde finished this prime minister's term after his death in office.

swap.text: In some Commonwealth countries, the monarch is represented by this position's holder. In Australia, the holder of this position has the power to dismiss the PM and dissolve government.
swap.answerHtml: Governor-General [do not accept or prompt on partial answers]
swap.clue: John Kerr controversially exercised the formal power to dismiss Whitlam as this executive representative of the monarchy in Australia.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the history wars, a dispute over the treatment of Aborigines in Australian history.
question.text: The so-called "black armband" school of history has documented the genocide of aborigines on this island in the Black War. This island south of Australia was once called Van Diemen's Land.
question.clue: In 1996, Martin Bryant killed 35 people on this island.

swap.text: Eddie Mabo taught the Papuan Meriam language to children from these islands off the coast of Queensland's Cape York Peninsula. Together with the Aborigines, the Melanesian people of these islands form Australia's Indigenous community.
swap.answerHtml: Torres Strait Islands [accept Torres Strait Islanders; reject “Torres Islands”]
swap.clue: This strait, named for a Spanish explorer, is home to namesake islands populated by indigenous Melanesian people and located between the Cape York Peninsula and the island of New Guinea.

question.text: A landmark 1891 sheep shearers' strike led to the founding of this party under the "Tree of Knowledge." This party's later leaders included Billy Hughes and Gough Whitlam.
question.answerHtml: Australian Labor Party [or ALP; prompt on Labor Party with “of what country?”]
question.clue: This political party passed important social reforms under leaders like Bob Hawke and Gough Whitlam.

swap.leadin: The death of this state's senator Bertie Milliner allowed its premier to controversially appoint Albert Field, giving the opposition a majority and leading to "The Dismissal" of Prime Minister Gough ("goff") Whitlam.
swap.text: Name this state that was led for almost two decades by "the hillbilly dictator" Joh Bjelke-Petersen ("Joe BYELL-kee Petersen"). Eddie Mabo fought this state in a 1992 court case that struck down the concept of terra nullius.
swap.clue: In a battle named for the capital of this state, troops rioted for two days in November 1942 against Douglas MacArthur and their American allies.

question.leadin: An incredibly strong worker known as Crooked Mick appears in folktales about a mythical one of these places called the Speewah.
question.text: Name these places, such as Anna Creek and Victoria Downs. Subsidiaries of these places, prefixed with the word "out-," also name remote communities of Aboriginal Australians.
question.answerHtml: stations [accept cattle stations; accept sheep stations; accept outstations; prompt on cattle ranches]

swap.leadin: This man names the iron bar correcting for vertical magnetism in calibrating compass binnacles, but he is better known for a journey on which he was accompanied by the adorable cat Trim.
swap.text: Name this English cartographer who became the first man to circumnavigate Australia and identify it as a continent.
swap.clue: This explorer was a member of William Bligh's Second Breadfruit Voyage that successfully brought the crop to the Caribbean.

question.leadin: Matthew Brady, not to be confused with the American photographer, was known as a "gentleman" one of these people and was an enemy of Governor George Arthur. FTPE.
question.text: Identify this group of outlaws that included Ned Kelly.
question.clue: "Bolters" like John "Black" Caesar made up the first generation of this profession, whose later practitioners included Mary Ann Bugg and her lover, Captain Thunderbolt.

swap.text: The shootout where Kelly was captured occurred in this small town in Northeast Victoria. A plan to derail train carrying policemen was foiled by the efforts of hostage Thomas Curnow.
swap.clue: Kelly was captured in a shootout with police in this town in Victoria.
